title: Outlook for Mac: sensitivity label inheritance from email attachments
summary: The briefing's controls, licensing statements and roadmap facts are supported. It correctly reports the conflicting Mac availability documentation; one minor clarification should also acknowledge Microsoft's differing guidance about recommendations for manually labelled emails.

claims.claim: Outlook for Mac can select a Purview sensitivity label for an email being composed based on its attached files' labels.
claims.quote: When composing an email in Outlook for Mac, Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels can be automatically applied or recommended based on the sensitivity labels of attached files.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes automatic application of an email label based on attachment labels.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels can be automatically applied or recommended based on the sensitivity labels of attached files.

claims.claim: The roadmap also describes recommending an email label based on attachment labels.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels can be automatically applied or recommended based on the sensitivity labels of attached files.

claims.claim: The roadmap item does not mention licensing.
claims.quote: This helps users consistently protect sensitive information, reduces manual labeling effort, and supports organizational compliance requirements by aligning email protection with the sensitivity of attached content.

claims.claim: Learn describes dynamically selecting the email label from attachment labels.
claims.quote: With this configuration, a sensitivity label is dynamically selected for the email message, based on the sensitivity labels that are applied to the attachments and published to the user.

claims.claim: Only attachment labels published to the user are inheritance candidates.
claims.quote: With this configuration, a sensitivity label is dynamically selected for the email message, based on the sensitivity labels that are applied to the attachments and published to the user.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; controls[0].governs; Governance controls
claims.claim: The highest priority attachment label is selected when supported by Outlook.
claims.quote: The highest priority label is dynamically selected when it's supported by Outlook.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Inheritance does not replace a manually applied email label, even when that label has lower priority.
claims.quote: When an email message has been manually labeled, that label won't be replaced by label inheritance from email attachments.
claims.fix: After this statement, add: 'Microsoft's Australian Government label-policy guidance also says that, when both inheritance options are selected, a manually labelled email can receive a recommendation to increase its sensitivity; the Office-apps page does not describe that exception.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/compliance/anz/pspf-label-publishing#label-inheritance, which says: 'In situations where a user has already applied a label, the second option comes into effect and recommend that the email's sensitivity is increased to match.'

claims.claim: Inheritance replaces a lower priority email label applied automatically.
claims.quote: Label inheritance from email attachments will replace a lower priority sensitivity label that is automatically applied or applied as a default label, but won't override a higher priority label.

claims.claim: Inheritance replaces a lower priority email label applied as a default.
claims.quote: Label inheritance from email attachments will replace a lower priority sensitivity label that is automatically applied or applied as a default label, but won't override a higher priority label.

claims.claim: Inheritance does not override a higher priority email label.
claims.quote: Label inheritance from email attachments will replace a lower priority sensitivity label that is automatically applied or applied as a default label, but won't override a higher priority label.

claims.claim: The attachment must be a physical file.
claims.quote: The attachment must be a physical file, and can't be a link to a file (for example, a link to a file on Microsoft SharePoint or OneDrive).

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Linked files, including SharePoint and OneDrive links, do not trigger attachment label inheritance.
claims.quote: The attachment must be a physical file, and can't be a link to a file (for example, a link to a file on Microsoft SharePoint or OneDrive).

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk and impact
claims.claim: By default, encryption from the automatically selected label is also applied to the email.
claims.quote: By default, if the automatically selected label applies encryption, the same encryption is applied to the email.

claims.claim: An inherited label configured for Do Not Forward also labels and encrypts the email with Do Not Forward.
claims.quote: If the highest priority label applies the encryption option of Do Not Forward, the email message is also labeled and encrypted with Do Not Forward.

claims.claim: If the highest priority label applies only user-defined permissions for Word, PowerPoint and Excel, no email label or protection is selected.
claims.quote: no label or protection is selected for the email message because Outlook doesn't support this label configuration.

claims.claim: A label must be scoped to both files and emails for attachment inheritance.
claims.quote:
Label inheritance from email attachments:

- For this configuration, the label must be scoped to both files and emails.

claims.claim: Label-policy settings apply to the users and groups to whom the policy is published.
claims.quote: As part of the label policy, you select users and groups to have sensitivity labels and label policy settings.

claims.claim: Files-and-emails scope is configured on the sensitivity label rather than the publishing policy.
claims.quote: On the Define the scope for this label page, the options selected determine the label's scope for the settings that you can configure and where they'll be visible when they're published:

claims.claim: Label priority is a label-level ordering setting that determines which attachment label wins.
claims.quote: When you've created all the labels you need, review their order and if necessary, move them up or down. To change the order of a label, select ... for Actions, and then select one of the reordering options, such as Move up or Move down.

claims.claim: The recommendation option becomes selectable after selecting the inheritance checkbox.
claims.quote: When you select this checkbox, you can then further select the following option: Recommend users apply the attachments label instead of automatically applying it.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Why it matters
claims.claim: Without the recommendation option, inheritance applies the label automatically without prompting the user to apply it.
claims.quote: Without this selection, the label is automatically applied but users can still remove the label or select a different label before sending the email.

claims.claim: Users can remove an automatically inherited label before sending.
claims.quote: Without this selection, the label is automatically applied but users can still remove the label or select a different label before sending the email.

claims.claim: Users can select a different label before sending an automatically labelled email.
claims.quote: Without this selection, the label is automatically applied but users can still remove the label or select a different label before sending the email.

claims.claim: The recommendation option prompts the user rather than automatically applying the label.
claims.quote: Set the value to Automatic (to automatically apply the label) or Recommended (as a recommended prompt to the user.

claims.claim: Recipients not authorised by the label's encryption settings may be unable to open the encrypted email.
claims.quote:
When a document, email, or meeting invite is encrypted, access to the content is restricted, so that it:

- Can be decrypted only by users authorized by the label's encryption settings.

claims.claim: Sensitivity labels in Office apps require a subscription edition of Office.
claims.quote: To use sensitivity labels in Office apps, you must use a subscription edition of Office.

claims.claim: Outlook for Mac supports sensitivity labels for on-premises mailboxes starting with version 16.112.
claims.quote: For Outlook for Mac, sensitivity labels are supported for on-premises mailboxes starting with version 16.112.

claims.claim: Learn lists the Information Protection role groups, including Information Protection Admins, for creating and configuring labels and policies.
claims.quote:
You can use the following role groups:

- Information Protection
- Information Protection Admins
- Information Protection Analysts
- Information Protection Investigators
- Information Protection Readers

claims.claim: A custom role group with the Sensitivity Label Administrator role is another documented option.
claims.quote: Alternatively to using the default role groups, you can create a new role group and add the Sensitivity Label Administrator role to this group.

claims.claim: Learn also lists Compliance Data Administrator, Compliance Administrator and Security Administrator role groups as alternatives.
claims.quote: Another option is to add users to the Compliance Data Administrator, Compliance Administrator, or Security Administrator role group.

claims.claim: Set-LabelPolicy works only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is functional only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies > policy > Edit Policy > Default settings for emails > Inherit label from attachments > Email inherits highest priority label from attachments reaches the inheritance control.
claims.quote: You configure this setting in the sensitivity label policy, on the Default settings for emails page. For the section Inherit label from attachments, select the checkbox Email inherits highest priority label from attachments.

claims.claim: Set-LabelPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AdvancedSettings @{AttachmentAction="Automatic"} configures automatic attachment label inheritance.
claims.quote: Example: Set-LabelPolicy -Identity Global -AdvancedSettings @{AttachmentAction="Automatic"}

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies > policy > Edit Policy > Default settings for emails > Inherit label from attachments > Recommend users apply the attachments label instead of automatically applying it reaches the recommendation control.
claims.quote:
You configure this setting in the sensitivity label policy, on the Default settings for emails page.
When you select this checkbox, you can then further select the following option: Recommend users apply the attachments label instead of automatically applying it.

claims.claim: Set-LabelPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AdvancedSettings @{AttachmentAction="Recommended"} configures attachment label recommendations.
claims.quote: AttachmentAction: Unlabeled emails inherit the highest priority label from file attachments. Set the value to Automatic (to automatically apply the label) or Recommended (as a recommended prompt to the user.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: The portal checkbox and AttachmentAction PowerShell setting configure the same sensitivity label policy behaviour.
claims.quote: For more information about this configuration choice, see Configure label inheritance from email attachments.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether an existing inheritance-enabled policy starts applying to Mac users after they update.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook Mac AttachmentAction existing label policy inheritance update automatically enabled default; opened sensitivity-labels-office-apps, sensitivity-labels-versions, release-notes-office-for-mac and Set-LabelPolicy; none states how an existing enabled policy behaves on a Mac update.

claims.claim: Mail-flow controls tied to an email's sensitivity label can apply based on its inherited attachment label.
claims.quote: Any mail-flow or DLP related controls that are tied to the email’s label (for example, those discussed in preventing email distribution of classified information) is applied based on the email's attachments.

claims.claim: DLP controls tied to an email's sensitivity label can apply based on its inherited attachment label.
claims.quote: Any mail-flow or DLP related controls that are tied to the email’s label (for example, those discussed in preventing email distribution of classified information) is applied based on the email's attachments.

claims.claim: Learn describes Double Key Encryption attachment-inheritance cases explicitly for Outlook for Windows.
claims.quote: When Outlook doesn't support DKE: If the highest priority label applies Double Key Encryption, no label or encryption is selected for the email message in Outlook for Windows.
